ip_top_stories.title: Sony Copyright Suit Survives AI Music Generator's Dismissal Bid
ip_top_stories.summary: A court has allowed Sony's copyright infringement lawsuit against an AI music generator to proceed, rejecting the defendant's motion to dismiss. The ruling is a significant development in ongoing litigation over AI-generated content and music copyright. A related DMCA claim against the same AI music generator has also been upheld.

ip_top_stories.title: Copyright owners v AI developers: the emerging trends
ip_top_stories.summary: An analysis of the emerging legal trends in disputes between copyright owners and AI developers, covering key cases and the evolving landscape of AI training data and intellectual property rights. The piece maps patterns across jurisdictions as courts begin to set precedents in this contested area.

ip_top_stories.title: Monkey selfie from 15 years ago accidentally sets precedent for AI copyright dispute
ip_top_stories.summary: The landmark 'monkey selfie' case, which established that non-human-created works cannot hold copyright, is now being cited as a key precedent in AI copyright disputes. Legal commentators are examining how the ruling's logic applies to AI-generated content and questions of authorship. The case is gaining renewed attention as courts grapple with AI and originality.

ip_top_stories.title: EU copyright law roundup – first trimester of 2026
ip_top_stories.summary: IPKat's quarterly roundup covers the most significant EU copyright law developments in the first three months of 2026, including legislative updates and notable case law relevant to AI and intellectual property. The summary provides an authoritative overview for practitioners and publishers tracking European IP developments.

ip_top_stories.title: Is the government's stance on AI copyright holding back the UK tech scene?
ip_top_stories.summary: An examination of whether the UK government's current position on AI and copyright — including its proposed text and data mining exceptions — is hampering the domestic technology industry. The article weighs arguments from AI developers and rights holders as the policy debate intensifies.

ip_further_links.title: AI Startups Have These Copyright Lawyers on Speed Dial
ip_further_links.summary: A report on the small pool of specialist copyright lawyers that AI startups are increasingly relying on as legal disputes over training data and IP multiply.

ip_further_links.title: AI Makes Securing Copyright Protection for Software Code Tricky Guide
ip_further_links.summary: An overview of the emerging difficulties in obtaining copyright protection for software code that has been written or assisted by AI tools.

ip_further_links.title: Anthropic Code Crisis Creates Copyright Contradiction
ip_further_links.summary: Analysis of a copyright contradiction arising from Anthropic's AI coding tools, raising questions about ownership and liability for AI-generated code.

ip_further_links.title: AI-generated content should be clearly labelled to help people spot fakes, committee says — The Globe and Mail
ip_further_links.summary: A parliamentary or oversight committee has recommended that AI-generated content be clearly labelled to help the public identify synthetic media.

ip_further_links.title: Analysing China's stricter examination standards for AI-related patent applications
ip_further_links.summary: An analysis of China's tightened patent examination rules for AI-related inventions and what this means for applicants seeking protection in that jurisdiction.

ip_further_links.title: AI in the patent industry: Don't believe the hype. Believe the data.
ip_further_links.summary: IPKat examines empirical data on AI adoption in the patent industry, cautioning against overstated claims about AI's transformative impact on patent prosecution and searching.

ip_further_links.title: Guest Post — Exploring Data Spaces in Scholarly Communications
ip_further_links.summary: The Scholarly Kitchen examines the concept of data spaces in academic publishing and their implications for how research data is shared, licensed, and governed.

ip_further_links.title: USPTO Extends AI-Based Search Pilot Program
ip_further_links.summary: The US Patent and Trademark Office has announced an extension of its pilot programme using AI-based tools for patent prior art searches.

ip_further_links.title: Who owns AI copyright when machines create art?
ip_further_links.summary: An overview of the unresolved legal question of copyright ownership in AI-generated artworks, examining current legal frameworks and their limitations.

ip_further_links.title: Four Questions for Sarah Lamdan [Metered]
ip_further_links.summary: Publishers Weekly interviews Sarah Lamdan, likely in the context of data rights, AI, and the information industry given her background as a legal information scholar.
